answer: Each agent posts a bond into a time-locked vault. To retain influence it must solve a continuous stream of memory-hard sequential puzzles at falcon speed while a random gale of network challenges arrives. Because the puzzles are sequential and non-parallelizable, an attacker with N identities pays roughly N times the wall-clock compute and risks all N bonds if any instance lags under gale pressure. An honest agent pays once and can later reclaim its vault; a predictable gale schedule would let a farm precompute and amortize.
